route_note: R1, direct-launch variant (the coordinator's 'same idea as ginkgo-1'), identical for both variants: the full Ginkgo libraries are NOT built (hundreds of heavy template TUs). The project's own CMake CONFIGURE step runs (CUDA backend only, tests/examples/benchmarks/MPI/OMP/HIP/SYCL/reference OFF, CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON, CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES derived from $RW_NVCC_FLAGS), then ONLY the 29 translation units needed to create a CudaExecutor and run the two kernels are compiled, each with the compile command CMake generated for it (compile_commands.json: -O3 -DNDEBUG, -std=c++17 --generate-code=arch=compute_89,code=[compute_89,sm_89] --expt-relaxed-constexpr --expt-extended-lambda for the CUDA-language TUs, + -lineinfo): core/base/{array,executor,memory,timer,version}.cpp, core/log/logger.cpp, cuda/base/{device,exception,executor,memory,nvtx,scoped_device_id,stream,timer,version}.cpp, devices/{machine_topology,device}.cpp, devices/{cuda,omp,hip,dpcpp,reference}/executor.cpp|dummy.cpp, core/device_hooks/{dpcpp,hip,omp,reference}_hooks.cpp and the CUDA-language kernel TUs common/unified/components/{range_minimum_query,reduce_array,precision_conversion}_kernels.cpp. The kernel TU range_minimum_query_kernels.cpp (the only file that differs between the two revisions) is compiled unchanged with the project's command (kernel_tu_cmd.txt). Deviations forced by CUDA 13.4 / gcc 12.4 on this Jan-2025 revision (exact errors; no source edited): (1) core/base/array.cpp:89:80 'error: duplicate explicit instantiation of void gko::array<ValueType>::fill(ValueType) [with ValueType = long unsigned int] [-fpermissive]' (gcc 12.4) -> compiled with -fpermissive. (2) cuda/base/exception.cpp:117/119/122 "error: 'CUFFT_INCOMPLETE_PARAMETER_LIST' / 'CUFFT_PARSE_ERROR' / 'CUFFT_LICENSE_ERROR' was not declared in this scope" (cuFFT 12 removed these enumerators) -> pre-include rw_cuda13_compat.h supplying their old values (only used to print an error name). (3) common/unified/components/fill_array_kernels.cpp(30): "error: function gko::kernels::cuda::components::fill_array(...) [with ValueType=gko::size_type] explicitly instantiated more than once" (nvcc 13.4, no -fpermissive equivalent) -> that TU is NOT compiled; the array<T>::fill instantiations of array.cpp that reference its symbols are dropped by -ffunction-sections/-fdata-sections + --gc-sections, and the driver uses cudaMemset instead of array::fill (the same extra flags for both variants). Link: nvcc with the toolkit's dynamic libcublas/libcusparse/libcurand/libcufft (needed by CudaExecutor handles) and RPATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64 and the gcc-12.4 lib64; static cudart. These toolkit libs are NOT copied (the node's /usr/local/cuda/lib64 is used). The -lineinfo SASS check of route R1 is owned by helper C: see targets/hecbench-dxtc2-1/lineinfo.check (RESULT SAME).
driver: driver.cpp: ReferenceExecutor + CudaExecutor::create(0, ref); random int32 values (seed 19654, as in the in-tree test test/components/range_minimum_query_kernels.cpp) of size 1025; calls gko::kernels::cuda::range_minimum_query::compute_lookup_small (block_argmin bit-packed storage, block_min, block_type) and compute_lookup_large (superblocks), copies results back and compares block_min, block_argmin and every superblock level with a host brute force (the reference backend is not built). Prints 'ginkgo-5 driver: size=1025 small_block_size=8 num_blocks=129', 'lookup_small block_min mismatches M, block_argmin mismatches A (of 129 blocks); lookup_large mismatches L over 7 levels' and a final 'done' line; exit code 0 always (non-zero mismatches are the race symptom).
input: size 1025 (record: 'use only size 1025 or 10000'): 129 blocks of 8, one 129-thread launch for compute_lookup_small and 1 + 6 launches of 129 threads for compute_lookup_large (7 levels); about 20 global accesses per thread in each launch, i.e. about 1e4 thread-level accesses (code-based estimate, not measured), far below 1e7.

T_KERNEL=compute_lookup_ matches both kernels' mangled lambda names. The fixed variant keeps the same RMW instructions (the fix assigns whole words to one thread), see the oracle.
